_comment: Each entry under `servers` is written in OpenCode's MCP schema
(https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/), which is the richest of the three.
scripts/lib/mcp-render.mjs translates it into Claude Code's JSON and Codex's
TOML, so there is one manifest rather than three that drift apart.
Two placeholder forms are available. `{env:VAR}` is left in the config for
OpenCode to resolve at runtime -- use it for secrets. `{install:VAR}` is
resolved by bootstrap at install time -- use it for machine-specific values
such as paths, which should not depend on the launching shell.
`requiresEnv` and `optionalEnv` are manifest-only metadata, stripped before
writing. `requiresEnv` lists variables the server cannot work without; if one
is missing the server is written disabled. `optionalEnv` lists variables that
only improve the server (higher rate limits), and never disable it.
A missing variable is a warning, never a fatal error: the server is written
with `enabled: false` so it cannot fail on every startup, and re-syncing
after the key is supplied enables it again.
To add a server: append an entry under `servers`. Nothing else to change.
